title: 101 machine learning algorithms for predicting mortality in critically ill patients with spinal cord injury and sarcopenia: a multi-database study.
summary: A random survival forest selected from 101 candidate models stratified retrospective mortality risk in spinal-cord-injury and high-sarcopenia ICU cohorts; C-index ranges were 0.88–0.91 in training and 0.62–0.70 externally.
ai_technology: Ten machine-learning algorithms produced 101 candidate mortality models; a random survival forest was selected by ten-fold cross-validation and presented as risk scores and nomograms.
organization: Sichuan Provincial Rehabilitation Hospital; Yunnan University; Kunming Medical University; Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine

evidence.tested: Retrospective MIMIC-IV data (7,904 patients) supported training and eICU-CRD supported external validation. Across spinal-cord-injury and high-sarcopenia cohorts, training C-indices were 0.88–0.91 and external C-indices 0.62–0.70; higher predicted risk separated survival groups.
evidence.unknown: External discrimination was lower than training performance. Retrospective database validation does not establish prospective utility or improved survival from use of the risk score.
evidence.ai_role: Ten machine-learning algorithms produced 101 candidate mortality models; a random survival forest was selected by ten-fold cross-validation and presented as risk scores and nomograms.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
